newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest seen warm, dry through Thursday.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest seen warm, dry through Thursday.

text.p: Most of the U.S. Midwest corn belt can expect highs in the 80s (degrees Farenheit) and little precipitation through Thursday but meteorologists disagreed on forecasts for much cooler weather next week.

Light showers were forecast for extreme southeast and northwest portions of the corn belt on Tuesday with rainfall amounts mostly less than one inch, said Joel Burgio, meteorologist with Weather Services Corp.
Southern Ohio and Indiana should see 0.10 to 0.50 inch with 30 percent coverage while South Dakota and Minnesota can expect 0.25 to 0.75 inch with 50 to 60 percent coverage.
"In between those two regions, which is most of the Midwest, it should be basically dry with maybe an isolated shower from today through Thursday," Burgio said.

Temperatures were expected to peak in the low 80s F across much of the region but long-range forecasts indicated a Canadian cold front would push across the region this weekend, bringing much cooler temperatures, he said.
Lows were expected to be in the 40s F but there were no signs of a frost, said Craig Solberg, meteorologist with Freese-Notis.

But Smith Barney meteorologist Jon Davis said temperatures would likely be normal Sunday through Tuesday, warming later in the week. Normal highs for early September are near 80 F and lows are typically in the upper 50s, he said.

Burgio said the cold front would bring scattered light to moderate showers toward the end of the weekend. But chances of rain increased in the eastern corn belt as Hurricane Fran approached the U.S. coast, meteorologists agreed.
"We believe that rainfall chances will be increasing as we move into the latter half of the week, especially in the eastern and southern portion (of the belt)," Solberg said.
"Coverage should be very good. If all things work out, it should be a good soaking event," he added.
